description:
Somos una plataforma multicanal de interoperabilidad que integra, organiza y visualiza información de distintas fuentes y proveedores. Facilitamos el intercambio de datos mediante comunicación P2P, A2A y P2A, para que personas, organizaciones y sistemas puedan compartir información de forma clara y útil.

Buscamos convertirnos en una fuente confiable de información para organizaciones que necesitan conectar sus datos y tomar mejores decisiones, como ONG, agroexportadoras y más.
summary: WOMBAT turns NISAR radar change into a verifiable answer to one question: which square kilometer should be checked first? Built for analysts preparing for El Niño rains on Peru’s northern coast, WOMBAT compares two compatible NISAR L2 GCOV scenes, measures observed backscatter change on a 1 km grid, cross-checks it with OPERA DSWx-S1 surface-water data derived from Sentinel-1, and measures roads near each observed change. A deterministic engine ranks the cells, while results are packaged as a chain of digitally signed blocks that can be independently verified and shared through resilient P2P and web channels. We tested the method using real NISAR scenes from a known flood in Thailand and four sites in Peru. WOMBAT supports preparedness with traceable observed evidence: it does not predict floods or issue alerts, and its current thresholds are demonstrative.
details:
What Exactly Does WOMBAT Do?

When heavy rainfall, flooding, and infrastructure disruption affect northern Peru, decision-makers need to know where to verify conditions first. El Niño has repeatedly caused severe flooding and disruption to transport and agricultural activity in Peru’s northern regions. At the same time, disasters can damage communication infrastructure and interrupt the information flow needed for emergency coordination.

WOMBAT turns satellite and geospatial observations into signed, traceable evidence events. Instead of sending unverified files through disconnected systems, every event carries its origin, location, timestamp, context, and integrity proof.

How does it work?

When an analyst, municipality, insurer, or emergency team opens WOMBAT, they start with one clear question: which area should we verify first? WOMBAT compares two compatible NISAR radar observations, measures surface change, and divides the territory into practical grid cells. If the satellite scenes are not scientifically comparable, the system rejects them instead of producing unreliable results.

Each cell is enriched with independent context, including new-water observations from NASA OPERA DSWx-S1 and nearby road exposure from OpenStreetMap. Our Rust-based engine combines these signals to prioritize the areas that deserve human verification first. All rules, thresholds, and weights remain transparent, so organizations can understand why a location was prioritized.

Finally, WOMBAT turns every result into signed and verifiable evidence. The information moves through a peer-to-peer network to the cloud, web dashboards, and field devices such as Raspberry Pi. This helps decision-makers access trusted evidence, coordinate faster, and keep critical information available even when connectivity is unstable.

Demonstrantion P2P:

What is the motivation?

Peru is highly vulnerable to climate and natural hazards. Regions such as Piura face flooding during El Niño, while rural communities often lack timely and reliable information during emergencies. Farmers, families, small businesses, and local authorities are often the most affected.

Our motivation is also personal: members of our team experienced the Chongos Bajo earthquake and understand how uncertainty and limited communication make crises worse. WOMBAT was created to make critical evidence accessible, trustworthy, and available to communities when they need it most. We want technology to help communities act earlier, coordinate better, and recover faster.

What benefits does it have?

  • Faster, Better-Informed Response: WOMBAT helps organizations identify which areas should be verified first, supporting faster inspections, resource allocation, and emergency coordination.
  • Trusted and Traceable Evidence: Every event preserves its source, location, timestamp, and integrity, helping municipalities, insurers, banks, and NGOs make decisions with greater confidence.
  • Resilient Access to Critical Information: Evidence can reach cloud services, web dashboards, and field devices through P2P communication, keeping important information available even when connectivity is unstable.

What is the intended impact of the project?

  • SDG 11 - Sustainable Cities and Communities: WOMBAT helps local authorities and emergency teams prioritize field verification and protect vulnerable communities during floods, landslides, and climate-related disruptions.
  • SDG 13 - Climate Action: By transforming satellite observations into trusted, actionable evidence, WOMBAT supports faster climate-risk response and more resilient decision-making.
  • SDG 9 - Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure: WOMBAT strengthens information resilience through P2P communication, cloud relays, web access, and edge devices that can operate under intermittent connectivity.

Potential Beneficiaries
Municipalities
Civil Defense teams
Insurers and rural banks
NGOs and agricultural cooperatives
Vulnerable communities across Peru and Latin America

Extra:

As a team, we decided to use different methods to implement it, such as creating the architecture and using figma prototypes to get an idea of ​​what we were creating.

System Architecture

Figma:

https://www.figma.com/design/YP7pj1EtzRiEode95fRzHP/NASA?node-id=151710-3&t=E2meLjTu5o0MTCZR-1

Additionally, we established clear roles within the team, maximizing our individual “superpowers” in programming and other skills. By leveraging everyone’s strengths and working together, we focused on creating maximum value and successfully completing the prototype.

What we found with real NISAR data?

• Thailand flood: 48.6% of the area dropped by 3 dB or more, against 2.7% in a pair with no event. In the pair closest to the OPERA passes, 239 of 305 changed cells were corroborated by OPERA.

• Peru (Piura, Tumbes, Huaraz, Jequetepeque): no extensive open water. NISAR records wet soil, a 0.5 to 1 dB signal.

• Radar noise matters: applying the 3 dB threshold pixel by pixel flags 17% to 27% false change in cells with no real change. Averaging to 100 m first removes it.

Tools:

-Rust - Core Protocol and Security : WOMBAT’s core is built in Rust to ensure performance, reliability, and secure evidence handling. We use Ed25519 digital signatures to verify the origin and integrity of every evidence block, ensuring that information cannot be modified without detection. Rust also powers the deterministic validation and risk-processing logic.

-libp2p - Decentralized Evidence Distribution: Using libp2p and GossipSub, WOMBAT enables peer-to-peer communication between publishers, cloud relays, field devices, and edge nodes. Instead of depending on one central server, verified evidence can move across a distributed network and reach the nodes that need it.

-Python - Geospatial Data Pipeline: Python powers the satellite-data preparation workflow. Libraries such as h5py, rasterio, and GeoPandas process geospatial files, analyze spatial changes, create grid cells, and prepare evidence inputs. ASF Search and Earthaccess support discovery and access to satellite data sources.

-Terraform and AWS - Reliable Cloud Infrastructure: Terraform defines the cloud infrastructure as code, making deployment repeatable and auditable. AWS hosts the WOMBAT relay node, which receives and distributes P2P evidence, while System Manager enables secure administration without exposing SSH.

- GitHub Actions - Automated Quality and Releases: GitHub Actions automates formatting, testing, validation, packaging, and release generation. Every release produces lightweight binaries for Linux, Windows, and Raspberry Pi, allowing users to run WOMBAT without downloading the complete source code or installing Rust.

- React and MapLibre - Live Decision Dashboard: React provides the web interface for analysts and decision-makers. MapLibre renders geospatial data on an interactive map, while the dashboard consumes WOMBAT’s HTTPS API to display the latest verified evidence, its source, status, and affected area.

- Raspberry Pi and Edge AI: A Raspberry Pi can act as an edge node, receiving verified evidence through P2P or HTTPS. It can preserve the latest local event and use lightweight local AI models to explain the evidence in accessible language for field teams.

How is our project creative?

WOMBAT combines technologies that are rarely used together in climate-response tools: satellite evidence, digital signatures, peer-to-peer communication, cloud APIs, web mapping, and edge devices such as Raspberry Pi.

Instead of relying only on a central dashboard, WOMBAT creates a distributed evidence network. Information can travel from satellite processing to a secure cloud relay, a web application, and field devices. This makes the system more resilient and allows critical evidence to remain available even when connectivity is unstable.

Our creative approach is not only detecting environmental change, but making it verifiable, portable, and understandable. Every event can be traced to its source, shared across different devices, and transformed into useful information for people making decisions on the ground.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

We considered scientific reliability, accessibility, and resilience. Satellite scenes must be comparable before producing evidence, and each result must preserve its source, location, and timestamp to avoid misleading decisions.

We also considered real operational conditions: limited connectivity, vulnerable rural communities, and the need to access information from both web dashboards and low-cost edge devices such as Raspberry Pi.

Finally, we considered trust and usability. WOMBAT uses signed evidence, transparent rules, and a simple interface so that technical data can support municipalities, insurers, banks, NGOs, and field teams without replacing human judgment
